items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: But then I left the next year and then that’s when Roscoe Mitchell and I think Joseph Jarman, Anthony Braxton I think, yeah. That’s when it was officially formed, the AACM.

ctx.x: Well before you left Chicago, is that when you had an interaction with the members of the AACM? Can you tell me about that?

Well it wasn’t the AACM when I was there. I left the year before the AACM was formed. But the year before that one of my mentors, Muhal Richard Abrams formed the, oh what was it – the Orchestra — Experimental Orchestra. So Roscoe and Joseph Jarman and Malachi Favors, we were all sort of playing in that orchestra, and formed small groups from that orchestra. But then I left the next year and then that’s when Roscoe Mitchell and I think Joseph Jarman, Anthony Braxton I think, yeah. That’s when it was officially…
Was their approach to music startling to you or just something —

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think Anthony Braxton joined that group for a while. ... Lee Konitz, Anthony Braxton.

ctx.x: So do you know why Chick and Dave left? I know that Chick and Dave ended up forming Circle.
Yeah, they wanted to do some things and they left. I think Anthony Braxton joined that group for a while.
Right, I saw them as a quartet.
